name: loom-clock
description: loom's clock piece: an agent's self-set wakes, recurring schedules and the household's lanes, on systemd user timers

loom.name: clock
loom.label: Clock
loom.description: Wakes an agent: self-set alarms, recurring schedules and the household's lanes assigned to an agent, through loom's runtime or a runtime-managed house task. Relays between agents are the runtime's.

settings.name: WAKE_LOCAL_AGENT
settings.label: The agent this machine runs sessions for
settings.hint: an agent's id; its lane files are in the repo below, and its wakes may run here. Every other agent's run in houses

settings.name: WAKE_REPO
settings.label: That agent's repo
settings.hint: an absolute path: its lane files, and where its sessions start (default: the home directory)

settings.name: WAKE_LANE_DIRS
settings.label: Lane directories in the repo
settings.hint: comma-separated; a house's -f may name only a .md file under one of these, and the page lists the first

settings.name: WAKE_DATA
settings.label: Where the clocks are kept
settings.hint: a directory: one per agent (spool, schedules, log), and the household's lanes and relay log

settings.name: WAKE_AGENTS
settings.label: Agents that may set their own wakes over loom's API
settings.hint: comma-separated agent ids (default: the local agent)

settings.name: WAKE_FIRE
settings.label: Where the local agent's wakes run

options.label: In a house when its prompt says it's ready, else here

settings.name: WAKE_MODEL
settings.label: The model a wake runs on, unless it names one

settings.name: WAKE_SESSION_COMMAND
settings.label: The command used by older recorded local sessions
settings.hint: only the legacy session monitor uses this command's program; new local work uses the runtime's model choice and body policy

settings.name: WAKE_STUCK_AFTER
settings.label: Minutes a session may wait on a permission prompt
settings.hint: a session the clock started that waits this long on a permission prompt is stopped, noted on its task and said once; default 10, 0 or off: never

settings.name: WAKE_TASK_COMMENT
settings.label: How a stopped session is noted on its task
settings.hint: a JSON list, {task} and {text} filled in; default ["taskstore", "comment", "{task}", "{text}"] when taskstore is on PATH; off: never

settings.name: WAKE_ALERT_COMMAND
settings.label: How the clock reaches you when a wake keeps failing
settings.hint: a JSON list; the message is added as its last argument (a chat webhook script, a push). Without it, only the log

settings.name: WAKE_FIRE_GATE
settings.label: A check before any wake runs
settings.hint: a JSON list; a non-zero exit defers every wake an hour (a standby that must not run its primary's lanes)

settings.name: WAKE_PREAMBLE_FILE
settings.label: The words every wake starts with
settings.hint: a file with {name} {where} {id} {kind} {created} {note} {lanes} {body}; default: the piece's own

settings.name: WAKE_DELIVERY
settings.label: How a wake reaches the agent

options.label: Delivered through loom (the runtime reaches its body)
The old way: the clock asks for a house itself

settings.hint: unset: delivered through the runtime; spawn selects only the compatibility house task path. Local work always uses delivery

settings.name: WAKE_DELIVER_TOKEN_FILE
settings.label: The clock's own token, to deliver with
settings.hint: a file holding a piece token of this clock's (loom token create --piece clock/<name>)

settings.name: WAKE_PRINCIPAL
settings.label: loom's runtime's principal command
settings.hint: verifies whom a body acts for (--verify) and hands over whom a delivered wake is for (--wake); default loom runtime principal

settings.name: WAKE_LOOM_URL
settings.label: loom's address, as this machine reaches it
